title: Close the four scope gaps the sweep's own gates found
verification: scripts/dev-setup.sh && .venv/bin/ruff check concierge scripts tests launcher && .venv/bin/pytest -q && ([ ! -x scripts/check-frontend.sh ] || scripts/check-frontend.sh)
context: Direct follow-up to improve-conditional-guards-sweep (complete on main at e9bf772, 504 passing tests). That cycle's own two end-of-cycle gates produced four findings -- security sec1 and quality q1, q2, q3 -- and managed policy accepted all four as known debt because every one fell below its auto-remediate bar (sec1 low, q1 low, q2 low, q3 medium against a >= high bar). The user reopened all four on 2026-09-15 with 'fix all 4 of these quickly: no deferrals', which is both the authorisation to fix them and an instruction that nothing here may be carried. Every task is origin remediation, so this is a SWEEP plan: plan.sweep is true, the deferral ledger is CLOSED, and any finding this cycle's own gates raise gets a single end-of-cycle decision rather than becoming a third sweep's intake. WHAT THE FOUR FINDINGS ARE, with full evidence and verbatim remediations in improve-conditional-guards-sweep.json's security_findings[] and quality_findings[] -- READ THE NAMED FINDING BEFORE IMPLEMENTING: sec1, the VPC_CNI_ENFORCEMENT regex matches enableNetworkPolicy = "true" inside an HCL comment, so commenting the line out leaves enforcement_problems() returning [] -- the auditor CONFIRMED this by executing the committed regex against the real eks.tf with the line prefixed '# '. q3, task 6's mechanical-guard index omits tests/test_eks_values.py's CHART_RECEIVERS/CHART_PROCESSORS/CHART_EXPORTERS, which carry the same self-labelled config.CHART_VERSION pin and the same staleness risk. q2, a stale line reference at tests/test_cli.py:286 pointing at conftest.py:305-313 when the fixture body moved to :330-363. q1, restored(*keys) in test_cli.py duplicates the pop/save/restore loop conftest.redirected performs inline. THE PRIOR CYCLE'S CONSTRAINT 6 DOES NOT BIND THIS ONE AND THAT IS THE ONLY SCOPE CHANGE HERE. That constraint said 'this is a hardening sweep, not a refactor', which is precisely why task 2 and then task 6 each declined to consolidate q1, and why the 7.6 reviewer rendered it accept-as-debt rather than a live defect -- its remediation reads 'if a future cycle is scoped as a refactor'. This is that cycle. What replaces it is constraint 1: the refactor must be behaviour-preserving on a fixture every test module requests by name, and prior-cycle task 1 reads REDIRECT_KEYS BY REFERENCE, so a rename there breaks a security isolation landed an hour ago. ALL FOUR SITES WERE RE-VERIFIED AGAINST e9bf772 BEFORE THIS PLAN WAS WRITTEN and every line number in the findings still holds: VPC_CNI_ENFORCEMENT at tests/test_eks_check.py:68, enforcement_problems at :146 with its single search at :152, the negative test at :635, helpers edited/named/mentions/tofu_main at :88/:101/:108/:141; the index's CHART_VERSION bullet at conftest.py:26-29 and the vpc-cni bullet right below it; restored at test_cli.py:283 with the stale comment at :286; redirected at conftest.py:330 with the scrub at :354 and the restore loop at :358. THE CALIBRATION LESSON THE PRIOR CYCLE ENDED ON IS WHY CONSTRAINT 4 EXISTS: not one of those four findings was a defect in new functionality -- every one was a GUARD OR INDEX NARROWER THAN THE CLAIM IT MAKES. The prior cycle shipped protections whose preconditions were unasserted; then it shipped assertions whose SCOPE was unasserted. Its constraint 8 forced every guard to carry a committed negative test proving it bites, and that worked -- six guards are sound because of it. sec1 and q3 are the two places that discipline reached the guard's behaviour but not the guard's INPUT SCOPE. So constraint 3 carries constraint 8 forward verbatim and constraint 4 adds the missing half. DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE, because the user asked for these four and only these four: the auditor's two recorded non-findings (chart_pin_problems at test_eks_check.py:163 passes if the pinned label appears at least once, so a PARTIALLY regenerated recording with mixed helm.sh/chart labels goes unreported -- the same defect class as sec1 in the sibling guard from the same task; and the undeduped `carried` in that helper's failure message). Neither is touched here. Both are named in this log so the next reader does not have to rediscover them.
constraints: BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING ON THE SHARED FIXTURE. REDIRECT_KEYS, redirected, redirect_env, write_env, Recorder and subparsers_action keep their names and their observable semantics. Every test module requests redirected by name, five read core.ROOT through it, and prior-cycle task 1 reads REDIRECT_KEYS BY REFERENCE to scrub the -O child's environment -- a rename or a semantic change there silently reopens a security isolation that landed an hour ago. The hoisted helper is an addition; nothing existing changes shape.

NO EDIT to deploy/eks/tofu/. eks.tf is read as text only. The single eks.tf authorisation the user granted on 2026-09-15 was spent two cycles ago and has not been renewed. Tofu identifiers, the state bucket and the state key are untouched.

Every fix must be a COMMITTED assertion that a normal green pytest run exercises, AND must itself be pinned by a committed negative test proving it bites. Handoff-only evidence -- 'run the mutation and report the output' -- NEVER satisfies an acceptance criterion: it does not survive into the graded diff. No mutation of a real repo file is ever committed. No skips, no xfail, no relaxed existing assertion, no lint suppression, and no test deleted or weakened to make room.

A GUARD'S SCOPE IS PINNED AS EXPLICITLY AS ITS BEHAVIOUR. This is the half of the prior cycle's constraint 8 that was missing and it is what all four findings being fixed have in common. A negative test that proves a guard fires on a DELETED setting does not prove it fires on a DISABLED one; an index that lists three of five inventories is false about the other two. Where a fix widens what a guard reads, the negative test must provoke it at the NEW edge, not the old one.
NO PRODUCTION FILE IS TOUCHED THIS CYCLE. All four fixes live under tests/. launcher/, concierge/, scripts/, docker/, deploy/ and frontend/ do not appear in the diff at all.

CROSS-TASK OWNERSHIP OF THE enforcement_problems CLAIM: the conftest.py index bullet describing enforcement_problems states WHAT is pinned (the one vpc-cni setting that makes the agent NetworkPolicy enforceable), not HOW it is matched, so it stays true after task 1's comment-stripping fix. Task 2 must not rewrite that bullet's enforcement_problems clause to describe comment handling, and task 1 must not edit the index -- the two tasks run in the same wave and cannot see each other's diff.

Pins unchanged: config.CHART_VERSION stays 0.41.0, the upstream pin stays 3.0.0 / commit 1755859a, and the astronomy-concierge image prefix, concierge/ package name, Compose project name and Langfuse prompt and trace names are untouched.

tasks.title: Make the NetworkPolicy enforcement guard immune to a commented-out setting
tasks.why: The guard the last cycle added to protect the agent NetworkPolicy passes in exactly the state the original finding was filed about -- enforcement switched off by commenting the line -- so it is currently false assurance rather than protection.

acceptance_criteria.text: enforcement_problems() at tests/test_eks_check.py:146 strips commented lines before matching, for BOTH spellings Tofu accepts (a line whose first non-space characters are # or //), so a commented-out `enableNetworkPolicy = "true"` is reported as a problem naming deploy/eks/k8s/network-policy.yaml. Strip whole comment LINES, not inline trailing comments -- an inline comment after a real setting must not disable the setting's own match.

The committed negative test test_the_enforcement_guard_names_the_manifest_the_addon_setting_makes_real at :635 gains a comment-out case for EACH spelling, built with edited(tofu_main(), 'enableNetworkPolicy = "true"', '# enableNetworkPolicy = "true"') and the // variant, alongside the existing inputs. Per constraint 4 the new cases must provoke the guard at the NEW edge: assert the returned problem names the manifest, not merely that the list is non-empty.
The existing `dropped` and `elsewhere` cases and their assertions are unchanged in form -- widening what the guard reads must not be paid for by loosening what it asserts.

The real-tree positive assertion still passes against the actual deploy/eks/tofu/eks.tf, which today has the setting live and uncommented, so enforcement_problems(tofu_main()) is still []. Verify by running it, not by reading it.
deploy/eks/tofu/ is absent from the diff (constraint 2), and so is tests/conftest.py (constraint 6 -- the index is task 2's file and its enforcement_problems bullet stays as written).
chart_pin_problems at :163 and its tests are untouched. Its at-least-once looseness and its undeduped failure message are recorded in plan.context as deliberately out of scope for this cycle.

The index's own trailing claim about how many bullets are paired with a committed negative test is still true after the additions, or is corrected to match. An index that miscounts itself is the same defect the whole plan is fixing.

q1: a single module-level helper in tests/conftest.py holds the pop-and-restore loop, and BOTH conftest's `redirected` fixture and test_cli.py's `restored` context manager call it. No copy of the loop body remains in either file. The helper takes the keys to scrub so neither caller's key set is hardcoded into it.

q1, the hard line: `redirected`'s observable behaviour is unchanged. REDIRECT_KEYS, redirected, redirect_env, write_env, Recorder and subparsers_action keep their names and semantics (constraint 1). Demonstrate equivalence rather than assert it -- a key absent from the environment before the block is absent after, a key present before is restored to its exact prior value, and redirect_env's write_env side effect still fires. Prior-cycle task 1 reads REDIRECT_KEYS by reference, so confirm that read still resolves.

q1's documentation half: the conftest.py docstring that currently tells the reader the shape is shared deliberately while the code is not becomes FALSE the moment the code is shared. Update it to describe what the file now holds. Same for any comment in test_cli.py making that claim.

q2: the cross-reference at tests/test_cli.py:286 no longer names a line range at all -- it cites the fixture by name and says where to find it in prose (e.g. 'in its fixture body'), so a future insertion above it cannot stale the reference again. Per constraint 4 this is the scope fix, not just the value fix: re-pointing it at :354-362 would go stale the next time anything is added to the top of conftest.py.

A committed negative test pins the shared helper's restore semantics and fails if the restore limb is removed: one key set in the environment beforehand and one key absent beforehand, asserted individually after the block. log.note: Phase 4.5 conflict analysis, all four classes, against e9bf772. LEXICAL: three predicted files across two tasks, all unique -- task 1 owns tests/test_eks_check.py, task 2 owns tests/conftest.py and tests/test_cli.py. SYMBOLIC: two real edges, both pinned from both sides. (a) enforcement_problems is EDITED by task 1 and DESCRIBED by an index bullet in task 2's conftest.py (grep confirms exactly one such reference) -- pinned by constraint 6, task 1 ac6 (conftest.py absent from its diff) and task 2 ac10 (test_eks_check.py absent from its diff); the bullet describes WHAT is pinned rather than HOW it is matched, so it stays true after the comment-stripping fix and neither side needs to touch the other. (b) REDIRECT_KEYS is REFACTORED AROUND by task 2 (ac5 hoists the loop that consumes it) and READ BY REFERENCE by the prior cycle's task 1, already on main: tests/test_smoke_queries.py:28 does `from conftest import REDIRECT_KEYS` and :297 builds the -O child's scrubbed environment from it. That is a live dependency of a security isolation landed an hour ago, which is why constraint 1 forbids a rename and task 2 ac6 requires confirming the read still resolves. SHARED INFRASTRUCTURE: none -- no task touches deploy/, docker/, .env.example, a lockfile or a CI file, and constraints 2 and 5 forbid the Tofu tree and every production file outright. TEST INTERFERENCE: none -- the two tasks' modules are disjoint and neither asserts on the other's output; tests/test_conftest.py holds the MIGRATED inventory over REDIRECT_KEYS and is read by task 2 but edited by neither. WAVE LAYOUT: one wave of two, in parallel. No dependency edge exists in either direction. q1/q2/q3 are deliberately GROUPED INTO ONE TASK rather than split three ways because they are lexically entangled across the same two files -- q1 spans conftest.py and test_cli.py, q2 is in test_cli.py, q3 is in conftest.py -- so splitting them would serialize into three waves what one implementer can do in a single pass over two files.

CODEX PLAN REVIEW DELIBERATELY SET OFF for this plan (plan_review: "off"), with the tradeoff stated at the go gate so the user could reverse it. The kind/size gate would have passed (2 tasks), and last cycle the review earned its keep -- 3 rounds, 9 findings, all 9 applied, including the four handoff-only-probe findings that became this plan's constraint 3. Two reasons it is off here and both are about this plan specifically rather than about Codex. First, the user asked for these four fixes QUICKLY, and a round costs 5-8 minutes of wall clock against a plan whose total implementation is a regex predicate, three index bullets, one hoisted helper and one comment. Second and more substantive: the remediations are not my invention. Each was produced by an independent skeptical agent reading the merged code -- the security auditor EXECUTED the failing regex against the real eks.tf before writing sec1's fix, and the quality reviewer verified q3's three omitted symbols against tests/test_eks_values.py -- and each is quoted verbatim into the ACs. The adversarial pass that Codex would provide has, in effect, already happened one gate earlier. What is lost is the check on my DECOMPOSITION rather than on the fixes, and the decomposition here is two file-disjoint tasks in one wave, which is the smallest non-trivial shape there is. The evaluator gate, the negative-test requirement in constraint 3 and the scope requirement in constraint 4 are all unchanged.
